lines.trans: I did not understand anything myself.
Katya, please forgive me.
Where did all these cockroaches come from?
I meant well, understand.
It is not about the cockroaches at all.
Love is not just beautiful words.
Love is genuine trust.
Katya, I honestly trust you.
And it is no longer about you.
Now I have doubts myself.
It is better for us not to date for now.
Forgive me, Denis.
We will definitely punish everyone.
This is from the hotel for the inconvenience.
And it is already impossible to go back.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I am with you.
My butterfly.
Take more air in.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'yourself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I came here for a real reason.
Fine, I will go up myself right now.
You yourselves asked for five kilograms.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I must not get nervous right now at all.
No, nothing.
Today we have a draw.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I must not get nervous right now at all.
I have no idea.
No, nothing.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'understood', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: I have no idea.
I am her boyfriend, got it?
What? I did not understand you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне нужно доверие, а не ревность.
examples.trans: I need trust, not jealousy.
With them, if you are jealous, it is bad.
Yeah? Come on then, let's go.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, what exactly am I ignoring?
What do you think, will she forgive me?
Very cool, she will definitely forgive you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'куда').

examples.trans: How do you know? Does it show already?
Where did these cockroaches come from?!
Where did all these cockroaches come from?

meanings.note: Prefix 'вз-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'яться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to appear, come from, undertake', paired with 'браться'.

examples.trans: Where did the goose come from?
Where did this goose come from?
Where did it come from in the cream?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do you have a conscience?
Everything's fine.
As you all know...

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'these', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What kind of nonsense is this?
This is a service for our guests.
This does not interrupt your rest.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'cockroaches' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are cockroaches in your kitchen.

examples.text: Быстро уберите всех тараканов с кухни!
examples.trans: Quickly remove all the cockroaches from the kitchen!
Can you get us some cockroaches?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'wanted', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Они хотели внести изменения в меню.
examples.trans: They wanted to make changes to the menu.
I meant well, understand.
I want coffee.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он ведёт себя как ревнивый парень.
examples.trans: He behaves like a jealous boyfriend.

examples.text: Я как будто в театр сходил.
examples.trans: It is as if I went to the theater.
And how should I react?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'better', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Did something happen?
Oh, I see that you received it.
We work better than everyone here.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'business' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I came here for a real reason.
Please make coffee for the tables.
What are you doing in there right now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').

examples.trans: We have become completely absent-minded.
I must not get nervous right now at all.
Chef, I only need a tiny moment in there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Strong contractions.
Take more air in.
Come on, everything is fine.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'love' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Любовь — это не просто красивые слова.
examples.trans: Love is not just beautiful words.
Love is genuine trust.

examples.text: Первый раз я запел про любовь!
examples.trans: For the first time I sang of love!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What kind of nonsense is this?
This is a service for our guests.
This does not interrupt your rest.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Excuse me, what exactly am I ignoring?
You are simply spying on me.
This is not just a monkey to you.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful').

examples.trans: Where are our beautiful rose petals?

examples.text: Любовь — это не просто красивые слова.
examples.trans: Love is not just beautiful words.
Look how beautiful you've become!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лово'). Common neuter noun meaning 'words' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Надеюсь, шеф ничего там не сломает.
examples.trans: I hope the chef does not break anything up there.
What is going on there, did the elevator break?
You fill my life with meaning.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, actual').

examples.trans: Love is genuine trust.
This is real success!
He is a true friend.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'верие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'trust' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ей нравится, когда ей доверяет парень.
examples.trans: She likes it when her boyfriend trusts her.

examples.text: Мне нужно доверие, а не ревность.
examples.trans: I need trust, not jealousy.
Love is genuine trust.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You should introduce a new service.
You are simply spying on me.
Oh, you little macaque monkey!

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'верять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'I trust', paired with 'доверить'.

examples.text: Ей нравится, когда ей доверяет парень.
examples.trans: She likes it when her boyfriend trusts her.
Katya, I honestly trust you.
I can trust you, right?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Katya, I honestly trust you.
Do you want me to tell you honestly?

examples.text: Всё честно, Лёха. Взрослые не умеют ждать.
examples.trans: It's all fair, Lyokha. Grown-ups can't wait.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Strong contractions.
My butterfly.
Come on, everything is fine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are almost there already.
How do you know? Does it show already?
The workday has already started!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Are you satisfied now?

examples.text: Ну что, Витя, теперь ты мой раб.
examples.trans: Well then, Vitya, now you are my servant.
Who is the master here now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'омневаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'I doubt', paired with 'усомниться'.

examples.trans: I have no doubt.
Nobody doubted it.
Nobody ever doubted it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are almost there already.
We work better than everyone here.

examples.text: Сейчас мы быстро наведём здесь порядок!
examples.trans: Right now we will quickly restore order here!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'for now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No, not very much yet.
I do not want to publicize it yet.
It is time for you to finally reach a calm agreement!

meanings.en: to date, to go out (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тречаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to date / meet', paired with 'встретиться'.

examples.trans: It is better for us not to date for now.
We've been dating for a month.
We meet often.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'язательно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: So, will we definitely win right now?
We will definitely punish everyone.
I'll definitely buy you a tank.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'we will punish', paired with 'наказывать'.

examples.trans: History will punish them.
Mum will punish him.
To punish the blind?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The grand opening is tomorrow.

examples.text: В нашем отеле действует новая услуга.
examples.trans: A new service operates in our hotel.

examples.text: Вы сможете посмотреть на работу шефа.
examples.trans: You will be able to watch the chef's work.

meanings.note: Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'of the hotel' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В нашем отеле действует новая услуга.
examples.trans: A new service operates in our hotel.
Our hotel must surprise the guests.
Welcome to our hotel!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The grand opening is tomorrow.
What kind of nonsense is this?
I accept that after breakfast.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'удобство'). Common neuter noun meaning 'inconvenience' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is from the hotel for the inconvenience.
Sorry for the inconvenience caused.

examples.text: Шум в зале создал большие неудобства.
examples.trans: The noise in the dining room caused great inconvenience.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Strong contractions.
We are almost there already.
Come on, let's breathe.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to return / go back', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.trans: And it is already impossible to go back.
I'll be back soon.
He came back home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'back', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Who did you just name?
And it is already impossible to go back.

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago!

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'возможно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: And it is already impossible to go back.
No, that's impossible.
It's impossible to work here.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to

examples.text: Мне нужно доверие, а не ревность.

examples.trans: We need time to understand everything.

We're having a good time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'so that, in order to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is with you, mommy, huh?

What kind of nonsense is this?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
